links.outcome: Readability of LLM patient education responses (FRES, FKGL, CLI) for NPC radiotherapy
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 had significantly higher readability than ChatGPT-4o, with a 25.6% reduction in FKGL and 27% decrease in mean sentence length; ChatGPT-4o was harder to read.
links.quote: DeepSeek-R1 demonstrated significantly higher readability compared with ChatGPT-4o, with a 25.6% reduction in FKGL and a 27% decrease in mean sentence length, making it more accessible for populations with limited health literacy.

links.outcome: Currency of evidence and guideline references in LLM responses
links.effect: Both models scored DISCERN 51-62 (good), but had deficiencies in evidence currency, guideline references, and long-term side effects.
links.quote: However, deficiencies were noted in the areas of evidence currency, guideline references, and long-term side effects.

screen.reason: Evaluates the raw performance and readability of ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 answering nasopharyngeal carcinoma radiotherapy questions without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
